title: Continuum behavior emerges from discrete randomizing conserving rules

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Continuum behavior emerges from discrete randomizing conserving rules

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Smooth continuum behavior, such as diffusion of density, emerges from discrete systems whenever small-scale apparent randomness washes out individual details and conserved quantities constrain overall features, as shown by block cellular automata whose average density follows the diffusion equation.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And much as in physical systems like fluids, what ultimately leads to this is the presence of small-scale apparent randomness that washes out details of individual cells or molecules—as well as of conserved quantities that force certain overall features not to change too quickly.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 9, “Fundamental Physics”; section “Conserved Quantities and Continuum Phenomena” (from p. 458), p. 464. Scope: discrete systems with conserved quantities and intrinsic randomness, such as particle-conserving block cellular automata and fluids

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch09-08: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.77

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The named block systems and many neighboring rules can be simulated with standard methods. This resolves concrete instances, but the proposed general sufficiency of randomness plus conservation requires sharper conditions or a theorem.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Enumerate representative conserving discrete rules, estimate their coarse-grained density fields, and compare those fields with diffusion-equation solutions as scale increases. Convergence under quantified mixing conditions supports the claim; persistent non-diffusive transport provides counterexamples.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
'Whenever' is broader than any feasible enumeration.

Apparent randomness does not uniquely specify the mixing assumptions needed for diffusion.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The block-automaton demonstration is fully specified and can be rerun: averaged density either approaches the diffusion equation or it does not. Hydrodynamic limits are proved for some related lattice systems, so the mechanism is not merely visual similarity. The word 'whenever', extended to fluids and arbitrary discrete rules, is wider than those checks.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Average the density of particle-conserving block cellular automata over initial conditions with a fixed coarse density profile and fit the result to the diffusion equation. Agreement in the stated randomizing, conserving case confirms the exhibited mechanism; a conserving randomizing rule whose coarse density does not diffuse, or a fluid whose continuum limit needs extra structure, limits the 'whenever'.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Long-lived correlations, which Wolfram notes in one of his own examples, can block an exact diffusion limit.

The universal quantifier covers fluids and every discrete conserving system, not only the illustrated block rules.
